claim: CA1: a flat MERV-13 panel at the fan's free-air face velocity would need 130 to 215 Pa, 2.4 to 7.8 times what the fan develops; the fan slows instead
law: Media resistance at 3.5 m/s against the 27.5 to 55 Pa shut-off
check: Operating point 341 to 1110 m3/h at 21 to 52 Pa (13 to 71 % of free air); UC Davis measured 142 to 154 cfm (241 to 262 m3/h) with one filter on a box fan, 29 to 35 % of the same fan with four

claim: CA1: one kit gives a measured CADR of 131 to 141 m3/h (model 171 to 555), so a 150 m3 ward gets 0.9 eACH measured (1.1 to 3.7 model) and needs 2 to 6 kits for 5 ACH
law: eACH = CADR / volume; UC Davis 1-filter CADR 77 to 83 cfm
check: The principle holds; measured, one panel gives 29 to 35 % of the four-panel CADR on the same fan; scored in CAR-OPT-001

claim: CA1: a collar fits 'ceiling fans' (scope in the team deck)
law: Ceiling fans have no shroud and spans of 29 to 54 in (ENERGY STAR); they develop almost no static pressure
check: The 12 to 24 in collar cannot reach a 29 to 54 in rotor, and a rotor with no shroud has nothing to seal to; a panel under it would be bypassed. Fixed: scope is shrouded fans (box, pedestal, wall) and duct openings; ceiling fans are excluded

claim: CA1: the optional clip-on UV-C LED strip adds pathogen reduction
law: Dose = mean fluence rate x residence time ~ P l / Q; D90 in air about 0.5 mJ/cm2 for SARS-CoV-2 (estimate) and 1 mJ/cm2 for typical viruses at 254 nm (Allen, Benner and Bahnfleth 2021)
check: Low-cost strip (6 x 10 mW): 0.0030 mJ/cm2, 1 % single pass, +0.07 eACH in the ward. High-power strip (8 x 65 mW, 18 W): 0.16 mJ/cm2, 53 % at best, and one LED of 40 to 65 mW reaches the ACGIH limit in 7 to 11 min at 1 m. Mean path 0.10 m for the strip at the fan face, 0.30 m (generous) for the high-power case. Fixed: UV-C module removed from the kit

claim: CA1: a 270 to 285 nm LED module would make no ozone
law: Ozone forms below about 240 nm, peak near 185 nm; Luminus UVC LEDs emit nothing below 240 nm
check: Holds, but the module is removed (X4)

claim: CA1: a 1 mm gap at the collar lets under 10 % of the air bypass the panel
law: Orifice leak in parallel with the panel; 1.44 m round a 16 in rim; worst case over fans and media
closed_by: CAR-CAL-001 section 7 (round a 20 in box fan face, 2.15 m: 1 mm 8 %, 5 mm 31 %)

claim: CA1: the silicone collar seals guards of different profiles (wire rims, moulded rims, clips)
law: Team risk list: 'collar seal integrity across non-standard fan blade profiles'
check: A stretched sleeve seals a round rim; flats, clips and oscillation heads leave gaps of several mm (X6). Test fit on 5 fan models (V7)

claim: CA1: silicone holds its properties in heat and humidity
law: Silicone sheet rated -80 to 500 F (-62 to 260 C), Zoro listing
check: Far above room conditions for temperature; humidity, compression set, tear when stretched and disinfectant resistance are not in the listing and are to test (V7)

claim: CA1: loaded, the airflow falls to 149 to 486 m3/h (2.6 times) and 53 to 175 m3/h (7.3 times)
law: Parker final resistance; UL dust-loaded filters 7.3 times clean
check: The flat panel runs near shut-off, so loading costs it more than CA2

claim: CA1: running near shut-off does not overheat the motor
law: UL Chemical Insights report 200: single-filter box fans, winding at most 92 C, no ignition
check: Covers box fans; pedestal and wall fans to check

claim: CA1: a smaller 12 in fan gives at most about as much filtered air as a 20 in fan through one panel
law: Free delivery scaled with swept area, same shut-off pressure (A4)
check: 12 in 502, 20 in 609 m3/h: the panel, not the fan, sets the flow

claim: CA3: a 2 in MERV-13 panel on a return grille stays near the 25 Pa (0.1 in w.g.) filter drop US DOE gives as optimum
law: US DOE Building America: filter drop about 0.1 in w.c. optimum; total external static 0.4 to 0.5 in
check: 400 cfm: 29 to 48 Pa; 800 cfm: 59 to 96 Pa. Above the DOE optimum of about 25 Pa at every flow checked; it cuts system airflow and risks coil icing; a 4 in panel or a second grille would be needed. Option not carried
closed_by: Fix noted in CAR-OPT-001; option not carried

claim: CA3: a return-grille cassette gives 340 to 680 m3/h only while the air handler runs
law: CADR = E1 x return flow x duty
check: Most target sites (tents, shelters) have no ducts; the added drop (X12) lowers the return flow, so the upper value is optimistic

claim: CA3: four 16 mm magnet cups hold the cassette on a steel grille
law: Pull force of the bought cup to its data sheet (to assess); cassette mass about 1 kg
check: Not on aluminium or plastic grilles; screw clips needed there
